2026-11-18.title: Wednesday of the Thirty-third Week in Ordinary Time
readings: Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God the Almighty
Holy, holy, holy Lord, mighty God!
2026-11-18.alt: Optional memorial: Dedication of the Basilicas of Sts Peter and Paul, Apostles.
2026-11-18.verse: He said to him, ‘Well done, good slave! Because you have been trustworthy in a very small thing, take charge of ten cities.’
theo: John is taken up through an open door in heaven and sees the throne, with the four living creatures singing day and night, “Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God the Almighty, who was and is and is to come”, and the twenty-four elders casting their crowns before him. This is the worship that never stops, and every Mass joins it in the Sanctus. All our work on earth finds its meaning before that throne.

Luke's parable of the pounds is told as Jesus approaches Jerusalem, because people thought the Kingdom would appear immediately. A nobleman goes away to receive a kingdom and gives each servant one pound (mina). Some trade and gain; one wraps his pound in a cloth. The point: the time between Christ's going and his return is a time to work faithfully with what he has given. “To all those who have, more will be given.” Small faithfulness now is preparation for great joy then.
outline: Ask: what does heaven sound like? Revelation answers: “Holy, holy, holy.”
Every Mass joins the song before the throne.
The interim is the time to trade with our gifts.
live: Sing or pray the Sanctus attentively at your next Mass.
Do today's smallest duty with great care.
2026-11-18.prayer: Holy, holy, holy Lord God Almighty, who was and is and is to come, let my life join the worship of heaven, and make me faithful in small things while I await your return. Amen.

quick: Heaven's worship never ceases; every Mass joins it.
The time until Christ returns is for faithful work.
2026-11-18.action: Do your smallest duty today with great care.
2026-11-18.question: What have I wrapped in a cloth and left unused?

homily: Dear friends, today John is taken up through an open door in heaven. He sees the throne of God, the four living creatures who sing day and night without ceasing: Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God the Almighty, who was and is and is to come, and the twenty-four elders casting their crowns before the throne (Revelation 4:8–10).

This is the worship that never stops, and every Mass joins it when we sing the Holy, holy, holy. At the altar we do not only remember heaven; we are united with it. All our work on earth finds its meaning before that throne.

In the Gospel a nobleman goes to a distant country to receive a kingdom and gives each servant a pound to trade with. To the one who made ten more he says: well done, good servant; because you have been trustworthy in a very small thing, take charge of ten cities (Luke 19:17). The fearful servant who hid his pound lost even that.

God has entrusted gifts to each of us: time, talents, faith. Let us not bury them out of fear. Offer your work to God each morning this week, and let your ordinary tasks become part of heaven's song. Amen.
kids: Children, in heaven the angels sing Holy, holy, holy. We sing it too at Mass! Use the gifts God gave you today: your voice, your hands, your smile.

intro: Heaven's unceasing worship gives meaning to our faithful work while we wait for the King.

q: And one called to another and said: “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.”
Day and night without ceasing they sing, “Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God the Almighty, who was and is and is to come.”
points.apply: Pray the Sanctus attentively at Mass.

sub: The King has gone and will return.
Small trust leads to great responsibility.
q: The LORD God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to till it and keep it.
He said to him, ‘Well done, good slave! Because you have been trustworthy in a very small thing, take charge of ten cities.’
points.apply: Do one small duty with great care.

sub: The one who hid lost even what he had.
Work with all your strength now.
q: Whatever your hand finds to do, do with your might; for there is no work or thought or knowledge or wisdom in Sheol, to which you are going.
I tell you, to all those who have, more will be given; but from those who have nothing, even what they have will be taken away.
points.apply: Use one gift you have neglected.

concl: Our small work joins heaven's great song.
Be faithful until the King returns.
2026-11-18.resolve: Offer your work each morning to God this week.
